Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
1.

Heard Sri Yogesh Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri B.P.Singh, learned A.G.A.
2.This is the second bail application.

First bail application of applicant was disposed of vide order dated 27.5.2024 with liberty to the applicant to approach this Court or learned Trial Court concerned as advised a fresh along with status of trial after reasonable period.

3.Applicant has approached this Court seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.58 of 2020,
under Sections 498A, 304-B of I.P.C, and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station-Sakeet, District-Etah.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is facing trial for the above referred offences and he is in jail since 9.7.2020 and he is husband of deceased.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that there is a dying declaration, wherein there are allegations against the applicant that he along with co-accused pour kerosene oil on the deceased and set her ablaze.

He further submitted that mother-in-law and father-in-law of deceased have been granted bail by a co-ordinate bench in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.36682 of 2020,
vide order dated 22.2.2022.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.36682 of 2020
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Other co-accused Pooja and Roopkishor @ Pintu have also been granted bail by a co-ordinate bench in Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos.4154 of 2022 and 17545 of 2022, vide orders dated 9.3.2022 and 26.5.2022 respectively

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos.4154 of 2022 and 17545 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: , however, learned counsel for the applicant is not able to show that above referred Dying Declaration was specifically considered in said order.

6. In pursuance of an order passed by this Court, learned Trial Court has submitted a status report dated 2.9.2024 that out of proposed 21 prosecution witnesses, two have been examined and still 12 material witnesses are required to be deposed.
7. Court also takes note that occurrence took place on 21.2.2019 and deceased died on 17.3.2020 and postmortem was conducted on 19.4.2020.

8. Learned A.G.A. submitted that out of proposed 21 prosecution witnesses, two have been examined and 12 material witnesses are still to be deposed as such there is a likelihood that in the event of bail he may influence the witnesses.
9. I have considered the above submissions.
10. Nature of allegations against the applicant are very serious.
On basis of Dying Declaration, it may be a case of culpable homicide.

However, at this stage, there is no alternative charge under Section 302 I.P.C.
11.
Court also takes note that 12 material witnesses are still left to record their statement.
12. Court also takes note that co-accused have been granted bail, however, as referred above, issue of Dying Declaration was not considered, except vaguely, therefore, it is not a case of parity.

13. Now, only factor which remains for consideration is that applicant is in jail since 9.7.2020 i.e.
about 4 years and 10 months, however, still considering that there are other material witnesses and considering nature of allegations is against the applicant (husband of deceased), there is a likelihood that in case he is released on bail, he will try to influence other witness, therefore, at this stage prayer for bail is rejected and this bail application is disposed of with a direction that if the trial does not proceed substantially within a period of eight months from today, applicant will be at liberty to approach this Court or learned Trial Court as advised along with status of trial.
14. Registrar (Compliance) to take steps.
